actions: Completed matched full 100-point tau_p sensitivity map for positivity/simplex-preserving exponential p integration and public Euler, 50 realizations per point.
Extended tau_p=0.001 to 500 paired realizations to quantify rare solver-dependent basin selection.
Screened finite slow routing versus instantaneous softmax over 5x5 T/tau_x and five finite tau_p values.
Expanded all 25 T/tau_x cells at tau_p=0.3 to 500 paired realizations and expanded the strongest screen cell T=0.1,tau_x=3 for tau_p={0.3,1,3}.

extreme_tau_0_001_500.interpretation: Rare solver-dependent attractor selection exists at the most extreme tested tau_p (2/500 paired realizations), but the dominant curve-level regime is unchanged; do not infer directional superiority from this 0.4% event rate.

interpretation: Positivity-preserving integration removes the low-above-0.01 negative-p/NaN defect while leaving convergence fractions unchanged at 99/100 grid points and pointwise median true endpoint error nearly unchanged.
Filtered last-above-threshold observables remain more solver-sensitive than true endpoints, reinforcing that the public arrays named final are not robust literal end-state observables.
The broad finite-horizon transition survives the solver change: convergence falls around tau_p 6-13 and is zero by tau_p=13.219 under these fixed conditions.
The 50-repetition screen produced apparent finite-tau advantages, but the 500-pair tau_p=0.3 confirmation found no T/tau_x cell with a beneficial bootstrap interval excluding zero.
Six of 25 tau_p=0.3 confirmation cells were significantly harmful; at the strongest screen location, tau_p={0.3,1,3} all remained unresolved at 500 pairs.

Within the tested stationary-query endpoint regime, evidence continues to favor query-dependent softmax-like reweighting as the main retrieval mechanism; a robust endpoint benefit specifically attributable to slow kinetics has not yet been found. This does not rule out transient, switching, noisy-query, or nonstationary benefits.

exact_next_action: Confirm the strongest non-tau_p=0.3 screen candidates with 500-1000 paired realizations (especially T=0.03,tau_x=3,tau_p=3; T=0.003,tau_x=3 across tau_p; and T=0.1,tau_x=0.1,tau_p=0.03/0.1). Then move beyond stationary endpoint retrieval: run common-random-number readout-time sweeps and query-switch/noisy-query perturbations to test whether finite astrocyte kinetics provides a reproducible transient/hysteretic filtering benefit over instantaneous softmax. Preserve the corrected true-endpoint collector and positivity-preserving integrator; keep public filtered endpoints only as an implementation-audit field.
